text:
maria: CI red on PR #842 — build-image job failing at push step. registry returns 403 during manifest upload, seen on Buildkite. Anyone seen this recently?

deploy-bot: Buildkite: job #842 (build-image) failed — push step -> 403 Forbidden. https://buildkite.example.com/builds/1234

josh: can you paste last ~20 lines of the kaniko/buildx log? also the Dockerfile diff if you changed it recently.

maria: here are the tail lines from the runner:
```
INFO[0000] Pushing image to registry.mycorp.internal/repo/service:pr-842
error pushing image: denied: requested access to the resource is denied
FATA[0005] failed to push to destination: Error uploading manifest: received unexpected HTTP status: 403 Forbidden
```
I did change the Dockerfile earlier today to add an ARG for BASE_IMAGE and switched some runs to use an unpinned tag (so FROM $BASE_IMAGE).

kevin: 403 during manifest upload is usually auth or immutability/policy. Two quick checks: 1) did the registry creds/secret rotate? 2) did we enable tag immutability on the internal repo last week? If immutable, pushing manifests for the same tag can be rejected.

anya: also sometimes a corrupted cache or mixed-layer build (due to ARG changing) makes kaniko produce a manifest that the registry rejects. Try a rerun with no cache or a full builder prune on the runner. I had a similar flake yesterday.

josh: we use kaniko on the runners (no docker daemon). kaniko picks credentials from the service account via Workload Identity; that shouldn't expire mid-job but worth checking. @maria can you rerun the pipeline and paste the full log if it fails again? I can bisect.

maria: reran: https://buildkite.example.com/builds/1235 — same failure. Pasting the minimal Dockerfile diff: 
```Dockerfile
- FROM my-registry/internal/base:latest
+ ARG BASE_IMAGE=my-registry/internal/base:latest
+ FROM ${BASE_IMAGE}
```
No other changes.

kevin: That explains it — using an unpinned tag that's resolved at build-time plus kaniko's layer reuse can create a manifest whose digest doesn't match what the registry expects when tag immutability is enforced. Registry returns 403 when a push would mutate an immutable tag. Workarounds: pin the base to a digest, or disable immutability for that repo (not recommended). Also try building with --no-cache so kaniko can't reuse cached layers that cause mixed manifests.

josh: good catch. Could also be that the runner cache has old layers for the same tag but different digest. If rollback of the Dockerfile (use the literal FROM my-registry/internal/base:latest) previously worked, that suggests cache vs manifest mismatch.

maria: I updated the Dockerfile to pin the base to a digest and added --no-cache to the build step, triggered a rebuild: https://buildkite.example.com/builds/1236

deploy-bot: Buildkite: job #1236 succeeded — build-image (push) passed. :tada:

anya: nice. Can we add a quick CI lint so PRs warn when they change FROM to an unpinned internal image? That would prevent this class of failures.

josh: agreed — i'll open a small GH issue and add a preflight check to the image build action.

maria: thanks all — saved the release window. :thumbsup:
